answer.reason: Suppose a fallback makes route 1 the start, and the next request then succeeds straight away on route 1 with no fallback. The mutant resets the start to route 0, so the request after that begins from route 0 even though route 1 was the last route to succeed. That breaks the rule that the next request begins from the route that most recently succeeded.

answer.reason: The requirement says the next start is the route that most recently succeeded. The mutant keeps the highest route index seen so far instead. So if a later fallback succeeds on a lower-indexed route (for example after wrapping around, or once a higher sticky route fails), the next request still starts from the old, higher route. This breaks the stickiness the requirement asks for.
